product_overview: A minimal, single-file Node.js/Express backend that exposes a Smart Home Control API for E2E testing. It uses in-memory state (no database) and provides health, device management, and reset endpoints for reliable test setup and teardown.
core_goals: Provide a lightweight Smart Home Control API suitable for E2E testing without an external database (in-memory state).
Expose deterministic endpoints for health checks, listing and updating devices, and resetting all devices to default states for test setup/cleanup.
Include basic validation and error handling (404 for missing devices, 400 for invalid fields).
Be deployment-ready with a simple Dockerfile and start script while keeping implementation in a single server.js file.

features.name: Health Check API
features.description: Endpoint to verify server status and uptime so tests can confirm the service is available before running E2E suites.
user_flows: GET /health -> Receive 200 with status "ok" and numeric uptime (seconds)
GET /health with server misconfiguration -> Receive 500 server error

features.name: Device Management API
features.description: CRUD-style operations (read + update) for smart home devices (Light, Thermostat, Lock) stored in-memory. Allows tests to read device state and modify device properties such as on/off, brightness, temperature, and locked.
user_flows: GET /devices -> Receive 200 with Device[] containing Light, Thermostat, Lock and their current states
GET /devices/:id with existing id -> Receive 200 with the Device object for that id
GET /devices/:id with non-existent id -> Receive 404 Device not found error
PATCH /devices/:id with valid body {"on":true} for a Light -> Receive 200 with updated Device object
PATCH /devices/:id with valid body {"temperature":72} for a Thermostat -> Receive 200 with updated Device object
PATCH /devices/:id with body {"brightness":"high"} (invalid type) -> Receive 400 Invalid fields error
PATCH /devices/:id with non-existent id -> Receive 404 Device not found error

GET /devices -> Receive 200 with Device[] -> PATCH /devices/:id with valid body {"locked":true} -> Receive 200 with updated Device -> GET /devices/:id with same id -> Receive 200 with Device showing locked=true

features.name: Device Reset API
features.description: Resets all devices in memory to their default states so E2E tests can reliably start from a known baseline.
user_flows: POST /reset -> Receive 200 with message indicating all devices were reset to defaults

PATCH /devices/:id with valid body {"on":false} -> Receive 200 with updated Device -> POST /reset -> Receive 200 with reset confirmation -> GET /devices -> Receive 200 with Device[] reflecting default states
POST /reset while an internal error occurs -> Receive 500 Server error
